profile.campus: Chandler, Maricopa County, Arizona (CyrusOne Phoenix-metro campus, PHX1-PHX8)
profile.address: 2705 South Ellis Street, Building 9, Chandler, AZ 85286
profile.reading:
Per CyrusOne's own facility materials and an aggregator listing dedicated to this specific building, PHX8 sits at 2705 South Ellis Street, Building 9, Chandler, AZ 85286, part of CyrusOne's roughly 2,000,000 sq ft, eight-building Chandler campus (PHX1 through PHX8) totaling a publicly stated 169 MW of IT capacity across the whole campus; that campus-wide MW figure is not confirmed as this individual building's own capacity, so it is not asserted here as a single-building number.

Wikipedia's entry on CyrusOne states the company acquired 55.9 acres in Chandler in September 2011 for data center construction, part of its early-2010s national expansion under then-parent Cincinnati Bell before CyrusOne's own 2013 IPO; the company was founded in July 2000 by David Ferdman and Larry Bursten, headquartered in Dallas, Texas, and was taken private in a roughly $15 billion deal when Kohlberg Kravis Roberts (KKR) and Global Infrastructure Partners (GIP) acquired it, closing in March 2022. Chandler's electric and water utility, Salt River Project (SRP), serves this part of the Phoenix metro; Arizona data centers' water-intensive cooling systems have drawn scrutiny from local outlets including the Phoenix New Times given the state's arid climate and ongoing water-supply debates, a regional context relevant to this campus though not a site-specific consumption figure confirmed for this particular building.

Chandler's broader appeal to data center operators, alongside CyrusOne, the same submarket has drawn large campuses from other hyperscale and colocation players, stems from Arizona's relatively low natural-disaster risk profile (limited seismic activity, no hurricane exposure), business-friendly tax treatment for data center equipment under state statute, and proximity to fiber routes linking Phoenix to Los Angeles and other West Coast interconnection points, factors industry trade press has repeatedly cited in explaining the Phoenix metro's growth as a secondary US data center hub behind Northern Virginia and Texas.

reading.body:
CyrusOne PHX8 is one building in an eight-building campus in Chandler, Arizona occupying roughly two million square feet with a published campus-wide capacity of 169 MW across all PHX1 through PHX8 facilities. The individual building's IT load is not separately published, so the campus figure cannot be attributed to PHX8 alone. Assuming an industry-typical density of 85 watts per square foot of technical space, the 2 million square foot campus would require roughly 170 MW, which aligns with the published campus figure, but this calculation remains an assumption about the actual distribution across individual buildings.

The campus holds TIA 942 Class 4 certification, which qualifies it for mission-critical enterprise and hyperscale workloads requiring high redundancy and fault tolerance. CyrusOne's ownership was transferred to KKR and Global Infrastructure Partners in March 2022, ending the company's public trading status. The property sits in Chandler, served by Salt River Project for power and water, in a region where water-intensive cooling has drawn local scrutiny given Arizona's arid climate, though site-specific consumption figures for PHX8 are not published.

Arizona has 56 mapped data center facilities, of which only four publish capacity figures totaling 512 MW, making Arizona the fifth-largest state by published data center capacity in this dataset. The Chandler campus ranks fifth among those four published facilities statewide, behind Northern Virginia and Texas as national hubs but positioned to serve West Coast interconnection via fiber routes to Los Angeles. The Phoenix metro's secondary-hub status reflects Arizona's low seismic and hurricane risk, favorable tax treatment for data center equipment, and growing competitive advantage in the Western US market for AI compute.
